STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white, square-ish plate with a flat centre and a raised rim band. No curved inner bowl wall is visible. Flat plate, square.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are 20-30 cm. The plate looks like a standard dinner plate, so about 25-27 cm.
b) Reference object: no fork or utensil is visible. The melon cubes are about 2.5 cm across, so the plate spans roughly 10 cubes. That gives about 25 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm (square), so area is about 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Melon (cantaloupe) cubes: about 10-12 cubes, roughly 2 cm each, mostly flat on the plate, about 1 cm thick on average. Footprint about 8% of the plate, so about 50 cm². Volume about 50 cm³ × 0.6 = 30 g... adjusting for the mound of cubes stacked up to about 2 cm, the estimate rises to about 60 g.
- Chicken breast (grilled, sliced/pounded): a round piece about 8 cm across and about 1.5 cm thick. Footprint about 50 cm², volume about 75 ml, density 1.0, so about 90 g.
- Romaine/lettuce leaves: mostly wilted greens with a dressing sheen, covering about 15% of the plate (about 95 cm²), about 1 cm thick. Volume about 95 ml, cooked-leafy density not applicable because they look raw, so use 0.15: about 15 g. Add dressing: about 5 g.
- Grilled eggplant pieces: about 6-7 chunks, each about 2.5 cm, total about 40 g.

Hidden layer: a thin base of greens under the chicken adds maybe 5 g, already counted above.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no significant base layer. Total food is light, a single plated portion.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Melon: about 34 kcal
- Chicken breast, grilled: about 165 kcal
- Lettuce with dressing: about 25 kcal (dressing raises the average)
- Grilled eggplant (with a little oil): about 60 kcal

Totals: melon 60 g (20 kcal), chicken 90 g (149 kcal), greens 20 g (5 kcal), eggplant 40 g (24 kcal). Total about 210 g, about 200 kcal.
